h1: The 7 Best Privacy Screens for Laptops and External Monitors, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 privacy screen filters for laptops and docked monitors compared on fit, aspect ratio, mounting style and price, from under $25.
summary: The SightPro Magnetic 14 inch 16:9 is the privacy screen to buy for a laptop you open and close all day, because the magnetic mount lets you remove it in seconds. The SightPro 15.6 inch is the standard-mount pick for the most common laptop size, the SightPro 14 inch 16:10 fits newer business ultrabooks, and the SightPro 24 inch covers a docked monitor.
intro: Most people order a privacy screen by diagonal size and discover too late that a 14 inch filter is not one size. A 14 inch laptop with a 16:9 panel and one with a 16:10 panel have different heights, and a filter cut for the wrong ratio either leaves a strip of open screen or overhangs the bezel. Aspect ratio is the number that decides whether a privacy filter fits.

So this ranking is built around fit and ease of use. We reviewed seven filters from their listings and spec sheets, comparing size, aspect ratio, mounting method and price bracket. Five are laptop-sized and two are larger desktop filters for people who dock, and we say so clearly for each one so you can match your own screen.

products.name: SightPro Magnetic Laptop Privacy Screen 14 Inch 16:9, Patented Removable Filter
products.verdict: The fastest filter to put on and take off, thanks to a magnetic attachment.
products.description:
This SightPro filter fits a 14 inch, 16:9 laptop and attaches with magnets, with a removable filter design the listing calls patented. Its $25 to $50 price is the upper end for laptop-sized filters.

It ranks first because the biggest practical problem with privacy filters is that they are annoying to remove. If you share your screen in a meeting or want full brightness at home, a tab-mounted filter is a chore. The magnetic mount solves it. It beats the 15.6 inch SightPro for daily users, though that one covers a more common screen size. The tradeoff is the 14 inch 16:9 fit, which is narrower than newer 16:10 laptops.

Buy it if you carry a laptop between office, café and home. Skip it if your screen is 16:10.
products.idealFor: Travelers and café workers who remove the filter often.

products.name: SightPro 15.6 Inch 16:9 Laptop Privacy Screen Filter
products.verdict: A proven, tab-mounted filter for the most common laptop size, priced under $25.
products.description:
This SightPro filter is made for 15.6 inch, 16:9 laptops and uses a standard removable tab mount. It sells for less than $25.

It ranks second because the 15.6 inch, 16:9 screen is the most common laptop format, so more buyers can use it. The tab mount holds the filter in place with adhesive tabs on the bezel, which is secure but slower to remove than a magnet. The tradeoff is convenience: you will leave it on most days, and you will notice the slightly dimmer picture.

Choose it if you have a 15.6 inch laptop and want a cheap, effective filter. Skip it if you need frequent on-off removal.
pros: Fits the most common laptop size
Tab mount holds the filter securely
products.skipIf: You take the filter off several times a day.

products.name: SightPro 14 Inch 16:10 Laptop Privacy Screen Filter
products.verdict: The right-shaped filter for a newer business ultrabook with a 16:10 screen.
products.description:
This SightPro filter fits a 14 inch, 16:10 laptop and uses a standard removable tab mount. It is sold for under $25.

It ranks third because 16:10 laptops have become common among business ultrabooks, and most cheap filters are cut for 16:9, so a correct-ratio option has real value. It sits behind the 15.6 inch only because that screen size is more widespread. The tradeoff is the same as the other tab-mounted filters: it is secure but not as quick to remove as the magnetic version.

Buy it if your 14 inch ultrabook has a taller 16:10 panel. Skip it if you have the older 16:9 shape.
products.idealFor: Business ultrabook owners with a 14 inch 16:10 display.

products.name: Laptop Privacy Screen 14 Inch, 16:9 Aspect Ratio, for Lenovo HP Asus Thinkpad Envy Xps
products.verdict: A low-cost 14 inch filter that lists its active area and the laptop lines it fits.
products.description:
This 14 inch, 16:9 filter lists a 12.2 by 6.9 inch active area and names compatibility with Lenovo, HP, Asus, ThinkPad, Envy and XPS laptops. It sells for under $25.

It ranks fourth because the published active dimensions let you check fit with a ruler before buying, which most filters do not allow. That is a real advantage for anyone unsure about their screen. It sits behind the SightPro filters because the brand is less established and the listing does not describe the mount. The tradeoff is certainty: a generic filter needs a careful measurement from you.

Choose it if you want to verify dimensions before ordering. Skip it if you prefer a known laptop-filter brand.
pros: Active area is published for fit checks
products.idealFor: Careful measurers who want a cheap 14 inch filter.
products.skipIf: You want a well-known privacy filter brand.

products.name: SightPro 24 Inch 16:9 Computer Privacy Screen Filter for Monitor
products.verdict: A desktop-sized filter for a laptop user who docks to a 24 inch external display.
products.description:
This SightPro filter is a 24 inch, 16:9 desktop monitor filter, not a laptop-sized one. Expect to pay $25 to $50 for it.

Fifth place fits it because it solves a different problem from the laptop filters above: protecting an external monitor when your laptop is docked. That is a common situation in open offices and shared spaces, and a laptop filter does nothing for the second screen. The tradeoff is mounting and size, since it is much larger and needs to be aligned and held securely.

Buy it if you dock to a 24 inch monitor in a shared space. Skip it if you only use the laptop screen.
pros: Same brand as the laptop filters
cons: Larger filter is harder to align
products.idealFor: People who dock to a 24 inch monitor in shared spaces.
products.skipIf: You only work on the laptop screen.

products.name: Vxaop [2-Pack] 22 Inch Computer Privacy Screen Filter (16:10 Aspect Ratio)
products.verdict: A two-pack of 22 inch 16:10 filters, enough for a pair of external monitors.
products.description:
This Vxaop set contains two 22 inch, 16:10 desktop privacy filters, for $25 to $50. It is intended for external monitors, not laptops.

It ranks sixth because the two-pack covers a dual-monitor desk in one purchase, which is cheaper than buying two single filters. The 16:10 ratio is less common on 22 inch monitors, so check your screen carefully. The tradeoff is the fit risk: a wrong ratio leaves gaps, and returns on filters can be inconvenient.

Choose it if you have two 22 inch 16:10 monitors. Skip it if your displays are 16:9.

products.name: 15.6 Inch Privacy Screen Filter for 16:9 Monitor, 1920 x 1080 Resolution
products.verdict: A cheap 15.6 inch filter matched to 1920 x 1080 screens, for trying a privacy filter.
products.description:
This filter is for a 15.6 inch, 16:9 screen with 1920 x 1080 resolution, and costs under $25. The listing gives no other detail, such as the mount or brand history.

It ranks last because the SightPro 15.6 inch covers the same size from a more proven brand at a similar price. This one is useful as a low-risk trial for people who want to find out whether they like a privacy filter at all. The tradeoff is less information about the mount, the finish and the viewing angle, so treat it as a budget experiment.

Buy it if you want to test a filter cheaply. Skip it if you want the safer SightPro.
pros: Low-risk way to try a filter
cons: Few details about mount or finish
products.idealFor: First-time buyers testing a privacy filter.
products.skipIf: You want a proven brand and clearer specs.

whatMatters.detail: Aspect ratio is the width to height relationship of your screen, such as 16:9 or 16:10. A filter cut for the wrong ratio will overhang or leave a gap. Find your laptop's ratio in its specs, and match the listing exactly.

Sizes are rounded, so a 14 inch laptop can differ from another 14 inch laptop. An active area measurement, like 12.2 by 6.9 inches, lets you check against your screen with a ruler. Measure the visible display, not the bezel.
Magnetic mounts snap on and off, while tab mounts use adhesive tabs on the bezel. Frequent removers prefer magnets, and permanent users prefer tabs. Check which style the listing describes.

Privacy filters narrow the viewing angle by darkening what is seen from the side, and they also dim the picture slightly from the front. You may need to raise screen brightness. Do not expect the screen to look exactly as before.

Laptop filters are small and light, while monitor filters are much larger and need to be aligned carefully. Docked users need a second filter for the external screen. A laptop filter does not cover a monitor.

faq.q: Will a privacy filter work on a touchscreen laptop?
faq.a: It can, but check the listing and your laptop. Some filters are thick enough to change touch response. If touch matters, look for explicit mention of touchscreen compatibility.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying one?
faq.a: Ordering by diagonal size only. Aspect ratio decides fit. A 16:10 laptop needs a 16:10 filter, even if the diagonal matches a 16:9 option.

faq.q: Is the magnetic SightPro worth it over the tab version?
faq.a: If you remove the filter often, yes. The magnet saves time every day. If the filter stays on, the cheaper tab version is just as private.

faq.q: How do I install a tab-mounted filter?
faq.a: Clean the bezel, attach the tabs to the filter, then slide the filter into place against the screen. Make sure it sits flat and does not press on the webcam. Remove any dust first.

faq.q: How do I clean the filter?
faq.a: Use a dry microfiber cloth. Avoid ammonia-based cleaners or heavy pressure. Store it flat when removed.
Check the listing and your laptop layout. Most are cut to the screen area, but a filter that overlaps the bezel can crowd the camera. The active area dimensions help you confirm.

finalTake: The SightPro Magnetic 14 inch 16:9 is the best privacy screen here for people who use a laptop in different places, because it comes off in seconds. The SightPro 15.6 inch is the budget pick for the most common laptop size, and the SightPro 14 inch 16:10 fits newer ultrabooks. If you dock to a bigger monitor, the SightPro 24 inch or Vxaop two-pack covers it. Check your aspect ratio before you order.
